question: A marketer asks Claude to add citations to a draft that Claude had already written from general knowledge. What is the main concern?
options: A) Claude is unable to add citations to text it has already produced earlier in a conversation.
B) Citations added afterwards cannot be formatted in the style that the publication requires.
C) Adding citations later makes the draft longer, which the publication's word limit forbids.
D) Sources found to fit finished text may not actually support the claims attached to them.
correct_answers: D) Sources found to fit finished text may not actually support the claims attached to them.
explanations: Incorrect. It will readily do so, which is precisely what makes the practice risky rather than impossible.
Incorrect. Formatting is adjustable and is not what makes retrofitted citations unreliable.
Incorrect. Length is a practical constraint and is unrelated to whether the citations support the text.
Correct. When the text comes first, the sources are selected to match wording that was never derived from them, so the citation can look right while supporting nothing.
